slides.h1: How far does your salary really go in another country?
slides.p: Exchange rates vs what money actually buys, in 164 countries.

slides.h2: What $1,000 changed at the market rate buys, at US prices
slides.p: In 156 of 164 countries, a dollar goes further than in the US.

slides.h2: ₹1 lakh a month, changed at the 2025 exchange rate
slides.p: But it buys the same average basket of goods and services as about £3,536 in the UK.
slides.small: Purchasing power parity (PPP): what the same things cost in each country

slides.h2: Same basket, very different place in the pay ladder
slides.p: ₹1 lakh is 6.7 times India’s median pay. £3,536 is 1.3 times Britain’s. The same rank in the UK would take about £18,000 a month.

items: Big-city rents: PPP is a national average, not London or Mumbai
Tax: every figure here is before tax
Things priced in dollars: with 30% of spending at world prices, ₹1 lakh is worth £2,737, not £3,536

slides.p: a year buys in India what £40,000 a year buys in the UK: a quarter of the ₹45.9 lakh it converts to.
slides.small: National averages; city rents for expat-standard flats are far higher

slides.p: Convert any salary between 164 countries and see where it sits against local median pay.
slides.small: Use PPP as a floor for a move to a dearer country, then do the tax sums.
